newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firmer but still in range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firmer but still in range.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled firmer and at session highs on local shortcovering and light trade buying, but prices are not expected to stray far from their recent trading range, dealers said.
"It looks like we're working into a bit of a range," a trader said, noting that the benchmark May contract failed to pierce Monday's high of 11.08 cents a lb or take out the low of 10.68 cents.
"Unless we reach those extremes it will be hard to draw any conclusions," he said.
A move over the recent high of 11.08 cents in May or 11.19 cents reached Feb 20 would "most definitely spark quite a bit of new buying," a dealer said.
But producer scale-up selling around 11.00 cents is likely to keep a lid on the market, analysts said.
CSCE May sugar closed 0.04 cent higher at 10.88 cents after trading from 10.90 to 10.77 cents. Deferred finished 0.09 to 0.07 cent firmer.
The May/July spread narrowed to 0.17 from 0.20 after the previous close.
Volume was estimated at 10,218 lots, down from Monday's official 30,202 lots.
Prices drifted in listless dealings for most of the session, with buying in the the May/July spread from 0.16 cent supporting the benchmark contract at 10.77 cents.
Speculative selling and scale up trade selling from 10.90 cents in May limited gains until late-session short-covering emerged to carry prices to the highs, floor sources said.

Dockworkers at Brazil's Paranagua port said there is a 90 percent chance that they will stage a 24-hour strike Wednesday. The workers met with port officials earlier today in an attempt to avoid the threatened strike over wage increases.
